newsitem.title: BULGARIA: SOCCER-ECONOMIC CRISIS HITS BULGARIAN TEAMS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ECONOMIC CRISIS HITS BULGARIAN TEAMS.

text.p: Bulgaria's economic crisis has not spared the country's soccer teams, many of which lack funds to restart the national football championship this weekend after the winter break, soccer officials said on Thursday.

"Half of the teams lack money to start (the spring half of) the championship and seven or eight teams have asked us to help them financially," Bulgarian Football Union (BFU) chief Ivan Slavkov told a news conference.
Bulgaria is suffering a severe petrol and grain crisis due to a lack of funds for imports.
Slavkov said the BFU was trying to ensure teams had fuel for their buses so that they could get to games.

Bulgaria will play a friendly against PAOK Salonika on February 26 after Turkish club side Fenerbahce refused the match. The team will also face Slovakia on March 11 in Sofia ahead of its April's World Cup qualifier against Cyprus.
So far in European World Cup qualifying group five, Bulgaria, semifinalists in the 1994 World Cup, have lost to Israel and beaten Luxembourg and Cyprus. They play Cyprus on April 4.
